problem: The second fresh-context accountant completed the live devnet UI workflow and export, but the paid invoice list still presents 800 under AMOUNT DUE while the detail correctly reports Amount paid and To pay is zero (ACC-R2-01). The report also found that expired approval events combine an explicit expiry label with the original present-tense sentence claiming to cover the current invoice version (ACC-R2-02). These are two remaining display-semantic contradictions, not failed payment or authorization operations.
userImpact: A finance reader scanning the paid list can interpret the settled 800 Test USD as outstanding. A reader of historical approval evidence must mentally reconcile a past-version expiry with a current-version sentence. Both issues weaken otherwise successful reconciliation and evidence comprehension.
proposedChange: For the existing one-invoice list, render AMOUNT PAID when the displayed invoice is paid and AMOUNT DUE while it is unpaid; derive the paid display value from settlement.amount when present, with the existing amount as fallback. Keep the detail, filter counts and actual records unchanged. For an approval already proven expired by the existing exact event-revision/credit-reference linkage, render a historical supporting sentence such as Approved 1,000 Test USD for invoice version 1; superseded by credit CN-204. Preserve its original title, explicit expiry annotation, immutable event object and exported JSON; only the visible description in Activity and Evidence changes. Non-expired or ambiguously linked records keep their existing detail. Change src/App.tsx only, with src/styles.css permitted solely if the longer monetary heading needs narrow-layout accommodation. This is improvement cycle 2, the last authorized cycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Before payment, the invoice list monetary column says AMOUNT DUE and shows the current unpaid amount, including 800 after the credit.

After payment, All payables and Paid views say AMOUNT PAID beside the actual settled 800 Test USD at desktop and 390 px. No paid-row label implies that 800 remains outstanding. To pay stays zero and detail Amount paid/Settled amount remains unchanged.

Only approval events with the existing unambiguous earlier-revision and actual credit-reference linkage receive historical supporting wording in both Activity and Evidence. Their visible descriptions do not claim to cover the current invoice version.

Current approvals and records with absent or ambiguous credit linkage retain their existing descriptions. Event titles, stored details, state, signatures and downloaded JSON remain unchanged; no inference from amount differences is introduced.
No API, server, program, authority, role, approval, credit, settlement, export format or document scope changes. The human-readable export enhancement ACC-R2-03 is deferred.

Typecheck and production build pass. Perform a targeted fresh-context browser regression for unpaid/paid column semantics and historical/current approval wording on desktop and 390 px, preserving the completed payment record when possible. Do not create unnecessary additional payment or reset operations solely for cosmetic verification.
tradeoffs: A state-dependent monetary heading is appropriate for the bounded one-invoice workspace. A future mixed paid/unpaid list should use an amount label with per-row settlement semantics; that generalization is outside this change.

The rendered historical description becomes an explanatory presentation derived from the event amount, version and exact linked credit; the original detail remains in immutable data and JSON rather than being rewritten.
Printable or spreadsheet evidence export remains deferred. Muted-text observations remain evaluation limitations rather than a new broad visual/accessibility redesign in this last bounded cycle.

The second review was fresh-context browser usability evidence with instructional isolation, not independent verification of the underlying devnet transactions or a production accounting acceptance claim.
